newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran slams U.S. vote on Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Iran slams U.S. vote on Jerusalem.

text.p: Iran on Saturday condemned a U.S. House of Representatives resolution calling on President Bill Clinton to reaffirm that Jerusalem must remain Israel's undivided capital, the Iranian news agency IRNA said.
Foreign ministry spokesman Mahmud Mohammadi said the move "unmasks the real face of those who claim impartiality in the so-called Middle East peace process", IRNA said.

Tuesday's decision also violated "the spiritual rights of Moslems over Jerusalem and would encourage Israel's expansionist designs", it said in a report monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.

"As long as certain countries continue to pin hope on America -- which is in fact the main backer and the real cause of the Zionist regime's expansionism -- to work for the rights of the Palestinian nation, it is inevitable that we are going to witness more and more blows to the political reputation and credibility of these countries," Mohammadi added.
Israel, which captured Arab East Jerusalem in 1967 and annexed it in a move unrecognised by the international community including the United States, has welcomed Tuesday's 406-17 vote.

The House vote, which does not oblige the Clinton administration to act, came as Egypt and other Arab countries struggled to resolve a peacemaking crisis between Israel and the PLO which erupted when Israel began work in March on a 6,500-home Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
The Palestinians, who regard East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state, have termed the resolution a declaration of war.
